Community Health Nursing Internship

Community health internship — 4 weeks of supervised practice in family health, home visits, camps and records.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the objectives of a community internship
  • Perform family and home care in the community
  • Conduct a school or community health programme
  • Maintain community records and reports

In simple words

The community health internship is four weeks of supervised practice. The student delivers care, teaches families and keeps records in a village or urban community.

Objectives of the internship

  • Apply nursing process to a family
  • Assess the community and its health problems
  • Provide antenatal, newborn and child care
  • Conduct health education and camps
  • Work with ASHA, Anganwadi workers and the community
  • Maintain the registers and reports

Activities in the community internship

  • Family visits with home assessment and nursing process
  • Antenatal and postnatal visits with follow-up
  • Immunisation sessions and growth monitoring
  • Screening for anaemia, hypertension and diabetes in community camps
  • School health programmes, health education and nutrition teaching
  • Home-based care of the old, disabled and sick
  • Epidemiological investigation and outbreak follow-up work
  • Community survey and the village map

Placement pattern

The student spends the week in the sub-centre and village, does field rounds with supervisors, and prepares records and the weekly report.

🔴 Supervision and safety

Work always under supervision, keep the family informed, respect privacy and confidentiality, and record every activity honestly. The final evaluation includes competence, attitude and record quality.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Community internship applies nursing process to the family and the community.
  2. Activities include family visits, antenatal care, immunisation and health education.
  3. Registers and reports must be complete, accurate and on time.
  4. Supervision and confidentiality are essential.
  5. School and camp programmes test health education skills.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Community survey and mapping come before planning.
  2. Volunteers are used and supervised, not replaced.
  3. Field rounds build skills in home assessment.
  4. The nurse connects families to referral care.
  5. Final assessment includes competence, attitude and documentation.

📌 Memory trick

Community internship: L-C-T-R — Learn the family, Care for mother and child, Teach, Record.

60-second revision

  • Apply nursing process to a family and community.
  • Deliver antenatal and postnatal care, immunisation and growth monitoring.
  • Teach families and school groups.
  • Keep registers, family folders and reports.
  • Work with ASHA and Anganwadi workers; respect confidentiality.

Test yourself

Community survey data is used first to:

Answer: A. Community survey findings guide priorities and planning of services.

The community health nursing internship mainly trains the student to:

Answer: B. Community internships focus on family assessment, care, education and records.

Family folders are used to:

Answer: B. Family folders give the complete family health record and continuity of care.

In the community, the student supervises volunteers such as:

Answer: B. ASHA and Anganwadi workers are community health frontline volunteers whom the nurse guides.

Confidentiality in community work means:

Answer: B. Community care protects privacy and confidentiality, especially in close communities.
